about.description:
LoopTools is a package for evaluation of scalar and tensor one-loop integrals
based on the FF package by G.J. van Oldenborgh. It features an easy Fortran,
C++, and Mathematica interface to the scalar one-loop functions of FF and
in addition provides the 2-, 3-, and 4-point tensor coefficient functions.

The [publication](https://inspirehep.net/literature/474106) associated with
LoopTools is: T. Hahn, M. Pérez-Victoria. Automated one-loop calculations
in four and D dimensions, _Comput. Phys. Commun._ 118 (1999) 153.
DOI: [10.1016/S0010-4655(98)00173-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0010-4655(98)00173-8)
about.summary: LoopTools: A package for evaluation of scalar and tensor one-loop integrals

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "2.16"

recipe:
  name: "looptools"
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://feynarts.de/looptools/LoopTools-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 4113467575db3a14405d62d9e516b3b90410b73ea8d20c8eb8d70a30fc5cc9cb
  patches:
    - use-STRIP-from-the-environment.patch
    - link-the-Fortran-runtime-by-name.patch
    - link-the-REAL-16-check-with-LDFLAGS.patch
    - pass-all-five-point-arguments-from-EgetC.patch
    - use-the-Cxx-compiler-when-called-as-fxx.patch
    - do-not-add-stdlib-libstdc-when-MathLink-is-not-found.patch
    - add-a-shared-option-to-build-a-shared-library.patch

build:
  number: 8
  skip: win

outputs:
  # Every output runs the same build and packages a different part of it, so
  # that no file is in more than one output and the outputs can be installed
  # alongside each other.
  - package:
      name: "looptools-devel"
    build:
      script:
        file: build.sh
        env:
          # fcc is used to link against both libooptools.so and libooptools.a.
          # The --shared build adds the linker flags to it that are needed
          # for the shared library on macOS, which do no harm for the static one.
          LOOPTOOLS_CONFIGURE_ARGS: --shared
      files:
        - include/looptools.h
        - include/clooptools.h
        - bin/fcc
        - bin/f++
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ compiler("fortran") }}
        - make
        - sed
      run:
        # fcc requires the existence of a C and C++ compiler to work
        - if: linux
          then: gxx
        - if: osx
          then: clangxx

    tests:
      - package_contents:
          strict: true
          bin:
            - fcc
            - f++
          include:
            - looptools.h
            - clooptools.h

      - requirements:
          run:
            - grep
        script:
          # configure falls back to double precision without an error if its
          # check for REAL*16 fails
          - grep -e "-DQUADSIZE=16" $PREFIX/bin/fcc
          # configure adds -stdlib=libstdc++ to the C++ compiler flags of fcc
          # if its check for MathLink is left unpatched, which is wrong for macOS
          - if grep -e "-stdlib=libstdc++" $PREFIX/bin/fcc; then exit 1; fi
          # The -fdebug-prefix-map flags of the build have a path of the build
          # machine, so are removed from fcc
          - if grep -e "-fdebug-prefix-map" $PREFIX/bin/fcc; then exit 1; fi
          - fcc --help
          - f++ --help

  - package:
      name: "looptools"
    build:
      script:
        file: build.sh
        env:
          # --shared is added by add-a-shared-option-to-build-a-shared-library.patch
          # as the author has removed builds of a shared library
          # c.f. https://github.com/hep-packaging-coordination/packaging-hep-simulation-stack/issues/4#issuecomment-2489198926
          LOOPTOOLS_CONFIGURE_ARGS: --shared
      files:
        - bin/lt
        - lib/libooptools.*
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ compiler("fortran") }}
        - make
        - sed
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("looptools-devel", exact=True) }}
      run_exports:
        # LoopTools has no ABI versioning, and the library has no version in
        # its name, so do not assume compatibility across LoopTools releases.
        # Releases have so far only been of the form x.x, but pin to x.x.x so
        # that a patch release would also be excluded.
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("looptools", upper_bound="x.x.x") }}

    tests:
      - package_contents:
          strict: true
          bin:
            - lt
          lib:
            - ooptools
          files:
            - etc/conda/test-files/*

      - files:
          recipe:
            - examples/
        requirements:
          run:
            - fortran-compiler
        script:
          - lt 1
          # The three-, four-, and five-point tensor coefficients use REAL*16
          - lt 1000 2000 9000 100 200 300
          - lt 100 200 300 400 5000 -2000 10 20 30 40
          - lt 0 0 0 0 0 250000 -12239.172 150000 25000 -31183.285 10000 10000 10000 10000 10000

          # The compilers in the run and test requirements do not set any
          # environment variables on activation
          - export CXX=${{ "g++" if linux else "clang++" }}
          - export CXXFLAGS="-I$PREFIX/include"
          - export FC=gfortran
          - export LDFLAGS="-L$PREFIX/lib -Wl,-rpath,$PREFIX/lib"

          - cd examples
          # Unlike for libooptools.a, the Fortran runtime does not need to be
          # linked by hand
          - $CXX example01.cpp -o example01 $CXXFLAGS $LDFLAGS -looptools
          - ./example01
          - fcc example01.cpp -o example01-fcc -looptools
          - ./example01-fcc
          - fcc example02.c -o example02 -looptools
          - ./example02
          # example03 needs the C++ standard library, so links only if the C++
          # compiler is used. f++ uses it for any source file and fcc only for
          # a source file with the .cc extension.
          - f++ example03.cpp -o example03 -looptools
          - ./example03
          - cp example03.cpp example03.cc
          - fcc example03.cc -o example03-fcc -looptools
          - ./example03-fcc
          # example04 only works if it shares the common blocks of looptools.h
          # with the library. On macOS a program gets its own copy of a common
          # block unless told to use the one of the shared library.
          - if: osx
            then: export LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS -Wl,-commons,use_dylibs"
          - $FC example04.F -o example04 -I$PREFIX/include $LDFLAGS -looptools
          - ./example04

  - package:
      name: "looptools-static"
    build:
      script:
        file: build.sh
        env:
          LOOPTOOLS_CONFIGURE_ARGS: ""
      files:
        - lib/libooptools.a
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("c") }}
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ compiler("fortran") }}
        - make
        - sed
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("looptools-devel", exact=True) }}

    tests:
      - package_contents:
          strict: true
          files:
            - lib/libooptools.a
            - etc/conda/test-files/*

      - files:
          recipe:
            - examples/
        script:
          # The compilers in the run requirements of looptools-devel do not
          # set any environment variables on activation
          - export CXX=${{ "g++" if linux else "clang++" }}
          - export CXXFLAGS="-I$PREFIX/include"
          - export LDFLAGS="-L$PREFIX/lib -Wl,-rpath,$PREFIX/lib"

          - cd examples
          - $CXX example01.cpp -o example01 $CXXFLAGS $LDFLAGS -looptools -lgfortran
          - ./example01
          - fcc example01.cpp -o example01-fcc -looptools
          - ./example01-fcc
          - fcc example02.c -o example02 -looptools
          - ./example02
          # example03 needs the C++ standard library, so links only if the C++
          # compiler is used. f++ uses it for any source file and fcc only for
          # a source file with the .cc extension.
          - f++ example03.cpp -o example03 -looptools
          - ./example03
          - cp example03.cpp example03.cc
          - fcc example03.cc -o example03-fcc -looptools
          - ./example03-fcc
          # libooptools.a is linked into shared libraries by downstream packages,
          # so it must be position independent
          - $CXX -shared -fPIC example01.cpp -o libexample01.so $CXXFLAGS $LDFLAGS -looptools -lgfortran

about:
  summary: "LoopTools: A package for evaluation of scalar and tensor one-loop integrals"
  description: |
    LoopTools is a package for evaluation of scalar and tensor one-loop integrals
    based on the FF package by G.J. van Oldenborgh. It features an easy Fortran,
    C++, and Mathematica interface to the scalar one-loop functions of FF and
    in addition provides the 2-, 3-, and 4-point tensor coefficient functions.

    The [publication](https://inspirehep.net/literature/474106) associated with
    LoopTools is: T. Hahn, M. Pérez-Victoria. Automated one-loop calculations
    in four and D dimensions, _Comput. Phys. Commun._ 118 (1999) 153.
    DOI: [10.1016/S0010-4655(98)00173-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0010-4655(98)00173-8)
  license: LGPL-3.0-only
  license_file: COPYING
  homepage: https://feynarts.de/looptools/

  feedstock-name: looptools
  recipe-maintainers:
    - matthewfeickert
